transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-05
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Oliver Hale (CTO, Garnet), Priya Singh (Platform Eng), Marco Ruiz (Data Privacy), Leah Kim (PM)

Auto-summary (brief): Align on onboarding steps for Q1 pilot, confirm infra constraints (on-prem k8s, data residency EU), agree to deliver runbook + SOC2 artifacts, schedule architecture deep dive, provision trial capacity.

Transcript:
[00:00:04] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call — say hi when you can, and we'll move into objective.
[00:00:12] Oliver: Hi all, Oliver here. CTO at Garnet. Thanks.
[00:00:15] Priya: Priya, platform team.
[00:00:18] Marco: Marco — privacy and compliance.
[00:00:20] Leah: Leah, product.
[00:00:24] Sofia: Great. So objective for today is a short ignition: confirm pilot scope, constraints, timeline, and immediate next steps so we can get infra and security checks started. We want a concrete plan for the first two weeks.
[00:00:36] Ravi: I'll also briefly outline how our Dedicated trial environment would look and what the k8s integration surface is.
[00:00:42] Leah: Quick note from product: pilot is customer-facing in-app chat and semantic search via embeddings for our knowledge base. We want the experience to feel snappy.
[00:00:50] Sofia: Great. Do you have any initial latency targets? P95 or p50?
[00:00:55] Leah: Ideally p95 under 250ms for non-streaming generation, embeddings should be under 100ms p95 if possible. Those are aspirational.
[00:01:03] Ravi: Okay noted. We'll put together expected numbers vs model choices. Quick question for infra — are you on a public cloud VPC or an on-prem cluster?
[00:01:12] Priya: We run a mix. Primary is our private cloud in EU (self-managed k8s on bare metal). We can open egress, but data residency is strict — logs and content must stay in EU.
[00:01:24] Marco: Correct. Any PII or customer transcripts need to be retained for 90 days and then purged. We also need to integrate to our KMS (Azure Key Vault) for secrets and keys.
[00:01:34] Maya: Thanks Marco, that's helpful. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and private deployment — we'll surface the integration notes.
[00:01:42] Oliver: Is there an on-prem agent or does Redwood ship a whole control plane? Need clarity on network layout.
[00:01:48] Sofia: Good Q. For Redwood Private we provide a control plane that can be configured to use customer network peering, or you can run an on-prem package. For this pilot we were thinking a short Dedicated trial that routes within EU and can be pinned to not leave region.
[00:02:03] Priya: Sounds reasonable. We prefer the control plane outside but all inference to run within our VPC or region. Can you do that?
[00:02:10] Ravi: Yes — we can route inference to regional endpoints or dedicate capacity in your region. For the trial we'll propose 2x A100-equivalent nodes, continuous batching enabled, and prefix KV cache. Note: our notes say KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash in older docs, haha.
[00:02:28] Leah: Ha, okay. On models — what are the options? We want open models but also minimal latency.
[00:02:33] Ravi: We typically recommend a curated model from our catalog — a 7B quantized variant for chat or a 13B if you need slightly better quality. We'll provide perf profiles. If latency is critical, we can also try a distilled small model.
[00:02:46] Oliver: How much effort for quantization? I assume Redwood handles infra-level setup?
[00:02:51] Sofia: We handle model onboarding for trial; quantization profiles we can recommend. If you want to bring your own model, we have a model onboarding checklist and we can run compatibility checks.
[00:03:01] Marco: On the security front — need to confirm: are audit logs available, and can they be shipped to our SIEM? Also, tokenization of PII — do you redact?
[00:03:10] Maya: Audit logs are available, and we support forwarding logs via syslog or S3-compatible endpoints. We also have PII redaction options; we'll share the doc with the exact fields and retention controls.
[00:03:22] Priya: Network question: we'll need a port list and CIDR ranges for firewall rules.
[00:03:27] Ravi: We'll send a Network Access Requirements doc — includes IP ranges, ports, and recommended NAT behavior. I'll add the k8s service account and Helm chart notes too.
[00:03:37] Leah: For QA — what observability will be in the trial? We want cost per token, latency per route, and per-user tracing if possible.
[00:03:45] Maya: Console gives per-route latency and token breakdowns. During trial we'll enable debug traces on a subset of requests for deep analysis. We also provide SDK hooks for tracing.
[00:03:56] Oliver: OK. On timeline — product wants pilot in the second half of January, with a go/no-go at the end of the two-week trial. Is that workable?
[00:04:04] Sofia: Yes, aim to start infra prep this week, run the pilot by Jan 18–31 window. We'll treat that as target.
[00:04:11] Priya: Does Redwood require a vendor security review questionnaire? We have a standard infosec packet — will that be an issue?
[00:04:17] Sofia: We expect to complete an initial security review; we'll provide a completed vendor packet and SOC2 summary. If there are bespoke items we'll route to security.
[00:04:25] Marco: Great. Also need key rotation policies documented; we operate on 90-day rotation.
[00:04:30] Maya: We'll include key rotation options and KMS integration patterns for Azure Key Vault.
[00:04:36] Ravi: Quick note about performance trade-offs — batching and cache improve cost but can increase tail latency. For a customer-facing chat we can configure small max batch sizes and a short batching window. We'll show a recommended config.
[00:04:47] Leah: Do you have an example config for the trade-offs?
[00:04:50] Ravi: Yes; we have a recommended presets doc — "interactive-low-latency" and "throughput-optimized". I'll attach and highlight defaults.
[00:04:58] Oliver: Any blockers from your side to get started?
[00:05:01] Priya: We need the runbook, the network IPs, and the SOC2 doc.
[00:05:04] Sofia: We'll deliver the runbook and network doc by 2027-01-07.
[00:05:08] Maya: I'll also create a dedicated Slack channel and invite the key contacts after the call.
[00:05:13] Marco: We'll send the compliance questionnaire back the same week.
[00:05:16] Leah: One more on data residency — what about backups and snapshots? Will they stay in region?
[00:05:21] Ravi: Yes, we can configure storage to be regional-only and disable cross-region backups for the trial. We'll document the backup policy.
[00:05:29] Sofia: Okay, recap of agreed next steps — runbook + network doc, SOC2 summary, schedule arch workshop, create Slack channel, and provision the trial cluster. Any additions?
[00:05:40] Oliver: That covers it. We'll prepare sample traffic and user stories.
[00:05:43] Priya: We'll also confirm firewall windows for initial deploy.
[00:05:47] Sofia: Perfect. We'll shoot for the architecture deep dive on Jan 12 — we'll send invites after the runbook goes out.
[00:05:54] Maya: I'll draft the invite and include agenda items: k8s integration, KMS flow, network ports, and perf expectations.
[00:06:02] Marco: Quick question about billing for the trial — how is that handled?
[00:06:06] Sofia: For a short Dedicated trial we bill a nominal trial fee to cover capacity, or we can provide credits depending on the pilot terms. I'll follow up with pricing options in the email.
[00:06:16] Leah: Thanks. If we can get the runbook and SOC2 by Friday, we can move fast.
[00:06:21] Sofia: Understood. Anything else from Redwood team?
[00:06:24] Ravi: Nothing more. We'll prepare a baseline perf spreadsheet and recommended config.
[00:06:28] Maya: I'll add the onboarding checklist to the shared folder.
[00:06:31] Oliver: Thanks everyone.
[00:06:33] Sofia: Thanks all, we'll reconvene on the architecture deep dive. Bye.

Notes and links referenced: 
- Onboarding runbook (to be sent): https://redwood.ai/onboarding/runbook (placeholder link)
- Network access doc (will include CIDRs, ports)
- SOC2 summary and encryption notes (will attach)
- Performance presets: "interactive-low-latency" / "throughput-optimized"

End of transcript.
